title: The key waits
rule: Told from the brass key's place on its hook inside the closed cupboard: dark slits of light and voices until the door opens on E4.
declares: E0-E3 known only through cracks of light and lettered sound
made: every shape HANDMADE cut paper in code (films/swarm/99-ways/kit/cutpaper99.py): polygons with hand jitter reduced to straight scissor facets, flat papers whose fibre is the LoC 1934 sheet's relative tone, one down-right paper shadow per piece

the cupboard door's inside (kraft planks, battens, brace, iron lock box) with four openings cut through: jamb crack, gap under the door, keyhole, knot hole; the view never moves, so the openings sit in the same place in panels P1-P6

the office behind (wall, wainscot, ticket window, wall clock straight across from the keyhole, pendant lamp, desk) and the agent (shirt sleeves, waistcoat, glasses, pencil) and the stranger (hat, coat) in cut paper
sound words ('scrape', 'step', 'click', 'creak') cut out of pale paper from the shared pen hand; the four lines in the shared cut-paper balloons (penlib.balloon_piece)
the key's own SERVICE tag on its string in the foreground of every panel (dim in the dark, lit after the door opens)
hand-ruled borders (penlib.border_mask); folio '02 / The key waits' (pen99.folio)

events.E0: P1 chair legs and his boots under the desk through the gap, 'scrape'; P2 his boots cross the gap, 'step', a sleeve passes the crack
events.E1: P3 the upper crack: her hat and face behind the ticket-window glass; the lower crack, below the counter: his shirt sleeve and waistcoat edge (he has stopped by the cupboard, head hidden by the door), his boots in the gap; question balloon tailed to her face
events.E2: P4 the keyhole frames the wall clock at 4:10; his answer tailed low onto his sleeve and waistcoat in the lower crack, 366 px below her face
events.E3: P5 her hat turning away in the window pane; thanks balloon tailed to her; his sleeve still below the counter
events.E4: P6 his body darkens the crack, 'step', the latch 'click'; P7 the door swung open on its left jamb, light, he looks straight at the key
events.E5: P8 pencil to his chin, eyes up, 'Well, here I am... and what for?'; the view (the key) has not moved

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

beat: the key's view as the door is reached and swung open: boots in the gap, the crack goes dark, the latch clicks, the door swings out on its left jamb in three steps, light floods, he looks at the key, then the pencil goes to his chin with his line
beat_frames: b01: closed; his boots cross the gap under the door (step)
b02: his body blocks the crack; the latch clicks
b03: the door swings open on its left jamb (12%), light comes in
b04: the door swings open on its left jamb (35%), light comes in
b05: the door swings open on its left jamb (65%), light comes in
b06: open: he looks straight at the key (E4)
b07: pencil to his chin, his line (E5); the key stays where it hangs

self_check.viewer_inside_cupboard: structurally verified: P1-P6 are the door's inner face with the same four openings at the same coordinates; P7-P8 keep the opened door's inner face at left, the cupboard jamb at right and the sill at the bottom
self_check.known_deviation: the key's view faces the door, which places its hook on the cupboard's back; page 01 P7 shows the key hanging on the open door's inner face. Not a canon field (the canon says only 'a hook inside the cupboard door'), noted for continuity readers.
self_check.pending: independent blind reading not run by the maker
